method.description: Threat Intelligence Engine v1.1 relevance filter for Baltic and Polish hybrid-threat monitoring.
rules: do not keep an item merely because it mentions the EU, NATO, a Baltic country or a location
do not keep generic cybersecurity material without hostile, regional or operational evidence
require Baltic/Polish context, hostile-actor context or NATO-Russia/Belarus threat context
retain concrete sabotage, cyberattack, espionage, GNSS, drone, border, infrastructure and military threat signals
retain Russia/Belarus-linked warnings and information-operation signals
remove culture, sport, lifestyle, weather, general crime and domestic-news noise
use boundary-aware word and phrase matching instead of raw substring matching
treat cyber and critical_infrastructure as conditional rather than automatically strong categories

items.title: PM: Estonia ready to immediately close border in case of Russian mobilization
items.summary: Estonia is preparing for possible security risks if Russia declares a general mobilization, with Prime Minister Kristen Michal saying the country could close its border immediately if the threat assessment warrants it.

items.title: Kaja Kallas: Russia using hybrid attacks to erode Europe's support for Ukraine
items.summary: The European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs, Kaja Kallas, said that Russia's increasing hybrid attacks, acts of sabotage, and stray drones are aimed at frightening the residents of European countries and deterring them from supporting Ukraine.

items.title: From denial to exploitation: how the Kremlin has adapted its climate disinformation
items.summary: In the latest wave of climate-related narratives spread by the Kremlin, climate change is a vehicle to reinforce familiar disinformation tropes: the alleged authoritarianism and hypocrisy of the EU, Europe's supposed self-inflicted decline through sanctions against Russia, and, ultimately, the claim that Europe has no choice but to restore relations with Russia as a supplier of affordable oil and gas. The post From denial to exploitation: how the Kremlin has adapted its climate disinformation appeared first on EUvsDisinfo .

items.title: My home is not my castle: Kaliningrad as an address for Kremlin propaganda. Part 2
items.summary: In official discourse, Kaliningrad is increasingly portrayed as Russia’s western fortress: resilient, patriotic, and under constant external pressure. This article examines that tension between official narratives and lived reality. The post My home is not my castle: Kaliningrad as an address for Kremlin propaganda. items.title: My home is not my castle: Kaliningrad as an address for Kremlin propaganda. Part 1
items.summary: Kaliningrad Oblast is a Russian semi-exclave on the Baltic Sea, separated from mainland Russia and located between Lithuania and Poland – both members of the EU and NATO. items.title: Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s cultural heritage: a nail in the coffin of FIMI
items.summary: Russia’s strike on Kyiv Pechersk Lavra damaged a UNESCO site and exposed the Kremlin's disinformation narrative of protecting Orthodoxy, amid wider attacks on Ukraine’s culture. items.title: Explosives and propaganda: Russia’s dual-use drones
items.summary: Russian First Person View (FPV) drones have become a defining feature of the war in Ukraine. The same drones used to drop explosives on civilians and military targets are also being used to distribute propaganda leaflets in frontline communities, combining physical violence with psychological warfare. The post Explosives and propaganda: Russia’s dual-use drones appeared first on EUvsDisinfo .

items.title: How Moscow tries to cover up its failures on the Ukrainian battlefield
items.summary: As Russia's military gains slow and Ukraine intensifies strikes on key targets, the Kremlin is increasingly turning to exaggerated victory claims and disinformation to hide setbacks on the battlefield.
